title: Normalized State
definition: A database-like state structure where each item is stored uniquely under its ID in a dictionary object, and arrays of IDs are used to indicate ordering.
simpleExplanation: Deeply nested arrays are a nightmare to update in Redux. If you want to update Comment 4 on Post 3 by User 2, writing the immutable spread operators is horrific. Normalization flattens everything. You just do `state.comments['comment4'].text = 'New Text'`.
realWorldExample: Using `createEntityAdapter` to automatically normalize incoming array data from an API into a dictionary of `{ ids: [], entities: {} }`.

basic: What two keys are typically present in a normalized state slice?
intermediate: Why does normalizing data improve React rendering performance?

answers.question: Two keys?
answers.answer: `ids` (An array of strings for sorting) and `entities` (A dictionary object holding the actual data).

answers.question: Improve rendering?
answers.answer: If a child component only needs one specific item, it can connect directly to Redux via `useSelector(state => state.items.entities[id])`. When other items in the list change, this specific child component does NOT re-render because its specific item didn't change.
